Mar'dy bid farewell to his Saen companions and they continued on their journey. He stood in front of the ocean, the morning ocean breeze against his leathery scaled skin. He pondered his next move and the way the events had happened around him. He was so isolated in the ocean, he didn't know of titans and armies and gods. The things the Saen explained to him were fantastical and strange. A part of him longed for the adventure, to see these things with his own eyes. But he felt a strange calling back to ocean. Every time he looked at it, it seemed to look right back at him. Telling him to not to escape. And yet the ocean would spell death for him.

He wasn't finished yet.

Perhaps it was his fate or his duty. If he wanted to show compassion, it had to start with compassion for his fellow, for the Lot'dy, and eventually the Naga. And thats why he entered the water, wading in until the waves splashed over his head, he took one final breath of air before submerging beneath the surface. Perhaps the last time he will feel the sensation of air.

He swam towards the Dire Vents, staying clear of hunting parties and slave catchers. On his way there he found some hunter's harpoons, forgotten in the sand. When he finally arrived, he made sure to blend in with the other slaves, then headed over to the building where they housed the gladiators. Two steward caste guards watched the entrance. Not for long, Mar'dy expertly harpooned them both into the wall. He entered the building and headed straight for the warden, who he dispatched with a kick to the neck. Taking the keys, he started to free the gladiators, who freed each other and headed to the armory. Within a matter of minutes, the gladiators were armed and freed, ready to fight for Mar'dy (who they grew to respect from his previous life).

He lead them out on the street, where the Lot'dy around them quickly joined their cause. Many Stewards also joined them, perhaps from feeling the whips lash from a superior, or because of fear. Any stewards that resisted were trampled by the quickly building mob. Once the entirety of the burrows of the Dire Vents were freed, which happened in a mere hour, Mar'dy marched the giant mob to the Naga Fortress.

The Fortress was silent, the cold green stone menacing over them still. And for a moment the mob was silent too, watching Mar'dy just a few steps ahead of them. Surely the Naga knew what was happening, Mar'dy thought. Why are they hiding inside?

And just as he thought this the gate opened and out poured about one hundred Steward Lot'dy, armed with hooks and whips, most of them shaking in fear. As they poured out, hugging the walls of the fortress, the gates shut again. A single Naga came out of a balcony and hissed:

"What are you waiting for, go quell the rebellion!"

The Stewards marched forward against their brethren in a shaky formation. Many were visibly defecating as they approached the horde of Mar'dy's army, several thousand strong. Mar'dy stood in the front and watched with a stark expression as they walked forward. Within 20 meters of Mar'dy they threw themselves on the ground. They grovelled for mercy on their knees, asking that Mar'dy spare them. They claimed repentance for what they had done. Mar'dy stood above them, watching them squirm and cry as so many slaves he had seen squirm and cry. But whenever the slaves squirmed and cried, the lashings didn't stop. The mob started to roar for justice, many throwing rocks at the stewards before him, and pushing other stewards from their own ranks to begging group before Mar'dy.

But Mar'dy remembered compassion. Had compassion not been shown to him, he would already be dead.

"You are Lot'dy like us. If you repent, who am I to punish you?"

The roaring mob was once again silent. Some were visibly upset at Mar'dy and some were ashamed. The silence was broken, "Mar'dy the Just! Mar'dy the Just!". Soon all the Lot'dy chanted this, with more fervor than ever. With this, he ordered for the siege of the Naga Fortress to begin.

A lone spectre, aimless and lost, wonders the ocean floor. It follows a scent, a scent of hope and a vast imagination for a brighter future.

Now though, the scent of hope had been pervaded by confusion, fear and uncertainty. The spectre quickened its pace.

At long last, the source was in sight. A lone miserable sea creature had started a rebellion, how curious. The sense of promise, of hope remained, but the crowd was steeped in hesitation and fear. A nudge in the wrong direction could collapse the entire rebellion, bring an end to this wonderful being of immense promise.

This the spectre would not allow. '

So the spectre sent a message only the leader of the Lot'dy's would comprehend. "Fellow life, you have great potential within you, but there may be dire times ahead. When worst comes to worst, call for me, and I shall do all in my limited power to assist you."

The spectre stayed nearby, gathering in the diffuse ocean light. One way or another, the spectre would act. It would be overstepping its bounds if it acted without request, for after all it was the right of mortals to choose their own destiny. This it knew, but did not care for.

For this individual was too great a price to be allowed to perish here on the ocean floor. The very least it could do, the spectre resolved, was to ensure that the leader would live.

What is the difference between a top loading and a side loading washer? Which do you prefer?

Side loaders use less water but break more often and are more expensive to repair.

Top loaders use more water but are more reliable and simpler in design, making them cheaper to repair.

As someone who repairs their own appliances, top load is way easier to repair.

8 years and the drive belt broke, cost me $20 while a repairman wanted ten times that.

Front load washers would seem to be a greater liability in the event of a failure of the waterproof seal.

One should also consider the functionality of each design. If the space allotted cannot accommodate a lid (which opens upwards) or a door (which opens forward) then you may be forced to choose one design.
With a side loader, you need to distribute the clothes evenly at the start or it imbalances and won't spin properly. You can't use them for one large item only, e.g. a pillow.
This post made me think of a new design: the top loading washer with a horizontal spinning axis... would grabbing clothes really be that difficult?

The side loading washer uses gravity to push water through the clothes and the top loader doesn't. Most side loaders wash clothes better than the worst top loaders. But like others are saying - their disadvantage is leaking water from the seal. I prefer a good top loader since they last longer.
Side load allows you to stack if you are desperate for space.
